podcast.title: Early Lo-Fi Recording Methods
podcast.body: Merrill Garbus, performing as Tune-Yards, began making music in 2006 with notably lo-fi recording techniques. Her first record was released on a used and recycled cassette, and all the music for it was recorded using nothing but a handheld voice recorder. "The first Tuneyards record was released on a used and recycled cassette. The music was recorded using nothing but a handheld voice recorder."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Genre-Defying Sound
podcast.body: Tune-Yards' music is considered impossible to categorize, blending numerous genres including alternative, indie pop, rock, funk, pop, folk, Afrobeat, and free jazz. Merrill Garbus also heavily utilizes loops and samples in her work. "It is impossible to categorize Tuneyards."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lo-Fi Recording Beginnings
podcast.body: Merrill Garbus, known as Tune-Yards, started making music in 2006. Her first record was uniquely released on a used and recycled cassette, with all the music recorded solely using a handheld voice recorder. "The first Tuneyards record was released on a used and recycled cassette."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Signing with 4AD
podcast.body: The unique and experimental nature of Tune-Yards' early work, including recordings made with a handheld voice recorder, led to a deal with 4AD. This UK-based label is renowned for its experimental alt-rock roster, which includes bands like The Pixies, Bon Iver, and The National, and is known for taking chances on innovative artists. "This led to a deal with 4AD, the wonderfully experimental alt-rock label out of the UK, that also took a chance with bands like the Pixies, Bonnie Verre, the National, and so many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Success in Indie Pop
podcast.body: Tune-Yards, originating from New England, has been creating "charmingly offbeat music" since 2006, achieving significant success within the Indie Pop crowd. "She's from somewhere in New England, and has been making some charmingly offbeat music since 2006, very big hit with the Indie Pop crowd."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unconventional Aesthetics
podcast.body: Tune-Yards' artistic approach extends to unconventional notions of spelling and capitalization in her work, reflecting her distinctive and experimental style. "The roster notions of spelling and capitalization are unconventional."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Tune-Yards, the project of Merrill Garbus, is characterized by its leader's unconventional notions of spelling and capitalization, adding to the distinctiveness of her artistic presentation. "plus her notions of spelling and capitalization are unconventional."
